title: Tree Shaking
body:
Dropping exports that nothing in the dependency graph actually imports — cutting scenes that never get performed. If you import one helper from a large utility library, tree shaking is what keeps the other ninety from shipping to the user.

It depends on ES module syntax (`import`/`export`), because those are statically analysable: the bundler can determine at build time what is reachable. [[CommonJS]] `require()` calls can be dynamic and conditional, so they generally can't be shaken. Side effects also block it — a module that mutates global state on import can't be safely dropped, which is what the `sideEffects` field in `package.json` is for. Happens entirely at build time, alongside [[Minification]].
